A sterling translation tailwind on NAV (+0.4) is roughly offset by the higher cost of debt and Feb-2026 dilution on FFO per share (-0.2) and a 30-Sep valuation date at the peak of the Bund rout (-0.2). Impact sum +0.1, scaled 0.0: p_up 50 because the last three interims were sold (-3.12, -1.13, -2.88) and the stock is +7.6% over 20 days into the print. abs_move 3.0 is the pre-released European base, above this low-vol name's 1.58% median.

new_in_release.expect: H1 FFO per share roughly flat against 4.30c (H1 FY26): rent roll +11.3% offset by cost of debt 2.5% -> 3.5% and ~6% more shares after the Feb 2026 raise. Direction unknown, small.

Adjusted NAV per share likely up from 124.78c: income-led valuation gain plus a GBP/EUR translation tailwind (1.1516 -> 1.1701), the reverse of last H1's -0.9% FX-driven fall. Risk: valuers widening yields at the 30-Sep bond-rout peak. Lean up.
Interim dividend increased for a 26th time, about +3-4% on 3.18c, consistent with policy. Expected, so neutral.
No formal guide; commentary on the EUR150m/EUR175m FFO targets and on rising debt costs ('costs of debt may rise'). A change is unlikely and its direction unknown.
LTV after EUR150m of acquisitions and the bond refinancing; likely in the high 30s. Unknown.

findings.finding: Sterling rose against the euro over the half (GBP:EUR 1.1516 at 31 Mar 2026 to 1.1701 at 30 Sep 2026, both rates from Sirius's own documents), so the UK portfolio translates into a higher euro NAV. That reverses the FX hit that cut last H1's adjusted NAV 0.9% and depressed its EPRA EPS (2.84c, with a EUR14.2m FX loss on sterling cash). Headline NAV and EPRA EPS therefore face an easy comparison.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: H1 FY26 (17 Nov 2025): adjusted NAV -0.9% on FX translation and pretax profit -6% on a EUR14.2m FX loss; the stock fell 1.9% intraday and -2.88% over the window. FY26 (1 Jun 2026): NAV +5.0% 'ahead of consensus', +0.25%.
findings.why_not_priced: The FX rate is public and analysts model it, so it is partly priced. NAV, though, is the line the market has visibly reacted to at Sirius interims (last year's FX-driven NAV fall drew the -2.9% reaction), and the trading update gave no NAV figure. If the NAV rebound were fully expected, the stock would not still trade ~6% below the last reported NAV (100.1p against 124.78c/1.1701 = ~106.6p).
findings.independence: The UK valuation read from Landsec's H1 to 30 Sep 2026 (an £88m surplus against a £6m deficit a year earlier, 13 Nov 2026) suggests UK valuers did not mark down over the half: https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/landsec-profit-more-doubles-rental-growth-boosts-outlook . FY26 rate and the H1 FY26 FX hit: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/sirius-real-estate-ltd---sre/results-for-the-year-ended-31-march-2026/9593228 ; https://www.ajbell.co.uk/news/articles/sirius-real-estate-raises-dividend-forex-loss-dents-interim-profit

findings.finding: Weighted average cost of debt rose from 2.5% (31 Mar 2026) to 3.5% (Oct 2026 trading update) after the EUR400m bond was refinanced with taps, and the share count rose ~6% after the Feb 2026 placing (~1.505bn implied by H1 FY26 FFO/share; ~1.592bn implied by PIC's TR-1). So H1 FFO per share likely grows far less than the 11.3% rent roll and may be flat against 4.30c.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: H1 FY26: FFO/share 4.30c against 4.29c (flat per share despite +6.6% FFO), with the stock -2.88% over the window; FY26 FFO/share +4.5%, +0.25%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the 3.5% cost of debt is in the 5 Oct RNS. What is not public is the per-share FFO print itself. The headline rent-roll growth (+11.3%) sets a higher implicit bar than per-share FFO is likely to clear, and a flat per-share FFO beside a double-digit rent roll is the 'quality of beat' risk. Sized toward 0 because the input was disclosed.
findings.independence: FY26 WACD 2.5% and the Feb 2026 raise dilution note ('dilutive impact of the February 2026 equity raise'): https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/sirius-real-estate-ltd---sre/results-for-the-year-ended-31-march-2026/9593228 ; share count from PIC TR-1: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/sirius-real-estate-ltd---sre/standard-form-for-notification-of-major-holdings/9842070

findings.finding: The 30 Sep 2026 valuation date sat at the peak of the euro bond rout: the 10-year Bund was near a 17-year high above 3.6% in late September, after ECB hikes in June and September to a 2.50% deposit rate. Vonovia's Q3 call (4 Nov 2026) guided 2026 portfolio values roughly flat, implying H2 giveback. That raises the risk of a smaller valuation gain on Sirius's ~75% German book than its income growth alone implies.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: H1 FY24 (Nov 2023, the last rate-shock half): -3.12% over the window. FY26 valuation gain EUR111.3m with 1bp of German yield compression: +0.25%.
findings.source_date: 2026-10 (page; the URL carries no date path)
findings.why_not_priced: Weak case: rates are public and the stock has already rallied from 90p (CEO purchase, 24 Sep) to 100.1p as Bunds rallied >20bp in October. Kept small because it is macro-to-company transmission. Sirius's own language ('bond and equity markets are challenging', 'costs of debt may rise') concedes the pressure but gives no valuation number.

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured history of this line at Sirius prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: all three are public RNS, and the stock has risen ~11% from the CEO's 90p. The CEO bought after the period end, knowing the H1 numbers to 30 Sep, so it is a weak signal that the interims hold no negative surprise. PIC's buying adds JSE-side demand that the UK short register does not show.
